approach:
Root cause: a job cut on an earlier unmerged job's branch has its dependency written nowhere, and nothing after a merge looks at the earlier pull requests that the merge carries. Fix in two parts, both in the PR link and landing code. (1) `PrLink` (pr.rs) gains a defaulted `base_jobs` field. It is found and recorded at landing, not at cut time. `land_pr` fills it for an open link with the other jobs whose open link head is an ancestor of the job's landing commit, using a new `pr::all_links`. The change description says plainly that the base is found at landing. (2) After `land_pr` sees its own link Landed, a new `close_carried_prs` (landing.rs) walks `base_jobs`, and through each earlier link's own `base_jobs` the rest of the stack. For each earlier PR it asks the host for state and current head. It skips any PR that is not open. It closes the PR, with a comment naming the merging PR and merged commit, only when that head is an ancestor of the merged commit or of the exact head the host merged. The second arm covers squash merges, which leave no ancestry. Closing uses two new PrHost methods, `pr_status` and `close_pr`, with default error bodies. Every failure is a PrReport.warnings entry; the merge, landing record and stored link are never undone.

Commit-shape table (the rule reads only ancestry; it never classifies commits). Earlier PR head kinds are: LAND = the job's landing commit, published by `athena land --pr`, so it is on the local branch; CAND = the off-branch early candidate that run/mod.rs:741-746 builds and open_early_pr pushes (early.rs:291,318), which is replaced by the landing commit only when `land_pr` runs for that job (landing.rs:206-212).
1. LAND head, C squash-merged (merged commit has main as its only parent): CLOSED via arm 2 (head is an ancestor of C's merged head).
2. LAND head, C merged by merge commit (merged commit descends from C's head): CLOSED via arm 1.
3. LAND head, with a records-only commit and an intervention commit between the earlier job and C: CLOSED. Ancestry ignores commit kinds.
4. Three-job chain A <- B <- C, links of A and B both LAND: both CLOSED, in either record order. Case 2 has only C->[B] and B->[A] stored, to show the walk.
5. CAND head (the earlier job was verified and landed locally but `land --pr` never ran for it; C is cut on the local branch, which holds the landing commit, not the candidate): LEFT OPEN. The candidate is a sibling of the stack, so it is never recorded as a base and neither arm holds. The change does not close it. The CHANGELOG states it and it goes to the user as an open question. A real-git test pins it.
6. Earlier head has a commit pushed since (host head differs and is not an ancestor, or is unknown to local git): LEFT OPEN. An ancestry error adds a warning naming the PR.
7. Earlier PR already merged or closed on the host: UNTOUCHED, no write.
8. Stack replayed by plan_rebase or resync under new hashes, so the old published head is not an ancestor: LEFT OPEN, no error.
9. Retry-after-block: the blocked attempt's own PR holds its candidate, as in 5, so it is LEFT OPEN. The landed retry's own PR is judged normally.
10. A close or status call fails: WARNING, the landing stands.

Scope: the only edits outside the listed deliverables are (a) one mechanical line `base_jobs: Vec::new()` at each existing PrLink struct literal in early.rs, after_merge_tests.rs, display.rs, drain.rs and external_calls.rs. Rust requires every field in a literal, and criteria 2 and 8 need the field and a compiling workspace. They change no behavior. (b) docs/design/native-pr-landing.md, the only doc that mentions pr-link and lists its fields (line 153), which criterion 7 requires updated. main.rs is left unchanged because the CLI already prints every `report.warnings` entry.

decisions.choice: Record `base_jobs: Vec<String>` on PrLink with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]. It is found at landing, inside `land_pr`, for an open link, by testing which other open links' heads are ancestors of `job.commit`. The doc comment and CHANGELOG say plainly 'found at landing'. A test asserts the stored link holds it after `land_pr`.
decisions.reason: `land_pr` runs for both a link it just published and one adopted from the early step, so one site covers both. It already holds Ancestry and StateDir, so `LandPr` gets no new field and its nine construction sites stay untouched. Ancestry is exactly 'built on that job's branch' and needs no trailer parsing, so it works before and after C0. Skip-if-empty keeps unstacked links byte-identical on disk.

rejected.option: Record the base where the link is created (open_early_pr, early.rs:311-323, or publish)
rejected.why: At that moment it is unknown whether the base is unmerged or what its head is. The only value on hand is the candidate's `previous_job` (run/mod.rs:768, chain.rs:16), which names only the latest landed job and also names jobs already merged. Passing it needs a new field on EarlyPr (2 literals) and LandPr (9 literals across tests and two crates). The head on that link can still be a sibling candidate, so the carried test would fail the same way. It would only move the guess earlier.

rejected.option: Compute the base job from git history in Athena::land_pr and pass it in a new LandPr field
rejected.why: After C0 commits carry no trailers; a new LandPr field breaks every `LandPr {` literal; detecting bases from history for landed jobs is out of scope.

rejected.option: Record the earlier PR number instead of the job id
rejected.why: The number is not known when the later job is cut; the job id keys into the state-directory link that holds number and head.

rejected.option: Record nothing and scan all open links after a merge
rejected.why: That is the 'no recorded dependency' behavior named as the root cause, and criterion 2 requires the field.

decisions.choice: Carried test: the earlier PR's head as the host reports it now is an ancestor of the merged commit, OR an ancestor of the merging link's head (the commit the host was told to merge). An ancestry Err counts as 'not carried' for that arm; if neither arm holds and one errored, leave the PR open and warn naming the PR.
decisions.reason: The brief's rule is 'every commit reachable from the merged commit'. The repository squash-merges (docs/system-facts.md host merge rules; docs/design/native-pr-landing.md), so a squash commit has main as its only parent and the earlier head is never its ancestor. Arm 1 alone would never fire in production. The merge is guarded by the head sha (merge call at landing.rs:253), so a head that is an ancestor of it has all its content in main. Using the host's current head means a later push to the earlier branch is judged too, and an unreachable new commit keeps the PR open.

rejected.why: Never closes anything after a squash merge, so stale PRs would stay.
Out of scope ('any rule other than all commits reachable') and could close a PR whose content a later job changed.

decisions.choice: Do not close a PR whose host head is the job's off-branch early candidate. Name this shape in the plan table row 5, in the CHANGELOG, and as a user question, with a real-git test that pins it as left open.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 7: the candidate commit (run/mod.rs:741-746) is never on the branch, so the brief's reachability rule cannot hold for it. Closing it needs another rule (for example 'the job's landing commit is carried'), which the brief puts out of scope. The user should decide. The recorded `base_jobs` field and the close step are what such a rule would extend.

rejected.option: Judge the job's landing commit instead of the PR head, found with landed_commit_for(git, job.commit, earlier_job, fingerprint)
rejected.why: Needs the earlier job's verified fingerprint from records, which `land_pr` does not hold. It adds a new rule beyond the brief and widens LandPr. Offered as a follow-up in the open question.

rejected.option: Pretend the shape is covered by the ancestry test
rejected.why: It would not be: both arms are false for a sibling candidate, and the test would only pass because the fake ancestry says so.

decisions.choice: Run the reconciliation at the end of `land_pr` whenever the link is Landed, including a run that finds the PR already merged. It never returns an error.
decisions.reason: Covers a merge made by the host's setting or by hand, and retries a close that failed earlier. Closed PRs read as not open, so repeats are idempotent. Both Athena::land_pr callers, the drain (drain.rs:3256) and the command (commands.rs:286), and the [parallel] max_concurrency mode reach this one function while holding the merging job's own lock.

rejected.option: Run only on the call that sends the merge request
rejected.why: A manual merge or a failed close would never be reconciled.
It takes only &dyn Host and has no ancestry or close capability; widening it changes its callers.

decisions.choice: Add PrHost::pr_status(number) -> PrStatus { state: PrState (Open, Merged, Closed), head } and PrHost::close_pr(number, comment), both with default bodies returning an error. GhClient overrides: GET pulls/N; PATCH pulls/N state=closed, then POST issues/N/comments. All three log HostOperation::ReadPr.
decisions.reason: Defaults keep the other PrHost implementors (crates/athena-core/src/test_support.rs FakeHost ~188 and EarlyFake ~418, gh/tests.rs RunHost) compiling with no edit. HostOperation is a closed list in athena-data that the watcher parses; client.rs rerun_failed already reuses an existing variant for the same reason. Closing first then commenting means a failed comment leaves the PR closed and the warning says so.

rejected.why: Forces edits to every fake in out-of-list files for no behavioral gain.

decisions.choice: Do not add LinkState::Closed or a carried_by field on the earlier link; the host's PR state is the authority.
decisions.reason: A new variant reaches every exhaustive match on LinkState (display.rs and others), and writing another job's link file would bypass that job's lock.

rejected.why: Widens scope and writes another job's link without its lock.

decisions.choice: The drain does not change. The closed earlier job fails to land on each drain pass exactly as it does today with the stale open PR. This is named in dependents and pinned by one test of confirm_existing_merge on an Open link whose PR is unmerged.
decisions.reason: Critic finding 10. PrLander::land (drain.rs:3255-3263) calls athena.land_pr, and landing_from_report (drain.rs:3271-3290) turns any error into NotLanded. After the later job merges, the local branch is resynced onto the squash (resync_tip, land.rs:163), so the earlier landing commit is gone from it. `landed_commit_for` fails, and the fallback confirm_existing_merge (landing.rs:359, called at :800) returns None for an unmerged PR, so the error is 'not landed'. That outcome is the same open or closed. A drain change is out of scope.

rejected.option: Make land_pr or confirm_existing_merge read the host status of every open link
rejected.why: Adds a host call to every landing and to confirm_existing_merge, which takes only &dyn Host; breaks the fakes' call counts for no change to the outcome.

risks.risk: The most common stale shape stays open: the earlier PR's head is still the off-branch early candidate because `land --pr` never ran for that job (table row 5). Neither arm of the rule can hold for it.
risks.mitigation: This is the safe side: nothing live is closed. The change description, CHANGELOG and a real-git test state and pin it, and the plan puts the extra rule to the user as an open question. The recorded `base_jobs` and the close step are where such a rule would plug in.

risks.risk: Some stale PRs stay open after rebase_job_branch / plan_rebase replays an earlier job's commit under a new hash, or when an earlier job's link was already cleaned (row 8).
risks.mitigation: Fails on the safe side: the PR is left open and a warning names it when the ancestry check errors. Detecting such PRs from history is out of scope. The CHANGELOG states the rule.

risks.risk: The earlier job's PR is closed while its stored link still says Open, so a later `athena land <earlier job>` or drain pass fails to land it.
risks.mitigation: No worse than the stale state (the drain already reports NotLanded for it; see the drain dependent). The host refuses a merge on a closed PR and land reports it. No new link state is added, to avoid touching every LinkState match.

risks.risk: A close succeeds and the comment then fails, leaving a closed PR with no explanation.
risks.mitigation: The comment is posted after the close; its failure becomes a warning naming the PR and saying it is closed. The warning text is asserted in the criterion 6 test.

risks.risk: Wrongly closing live work, for example an earlier PR with a newer commit not in the merge.
risks.mitigation: The host's current head is judged, not the recorded one; closing needs the PR Open and its head an ancestor. The head-e2, unknown-head and Merged/Closed tests guard it.

risks.risk: A concurrent process writes another job's pr-link.json while it is read ([parallel] max_concurrency path).
risks.mitigation: The step only reads other links; a read or parse error is a warning that skips that link; it never writes another job's file. The merging job's own lock covers its own link.

risks.risk: Editing docs trips the ontology or budget tests.
risks.mitigation: Add sentences only; leave marker lines (docs/ontology.toml:56,128,129) unchanged; run `cargo test --locked` before finishing.

risks.risk: A PrLink literal is missed, breaking compilation in a crate outside the listed deliverables.
risks.mitigation: The nine literal sites found by grep of `PrLink {` are all listed in dependents; the producer re-greps `PrLink {` and runs the full `cargo test --locked`, which fails to compile on any miss.

risks.risk: The real-git fixture drifts from the real branch shape.
risks.mitigation: It differs from the real repository in that candidates and landing commits are made with commit_tree and the land fixtures, not by a real `athena go`, and the host is a fake that reports scripted statuses. It keeps the properties the rule depends on: the off-branch candidate parented on the branch, landing commits on the branch, records-only and intervention commits between jobs, and a squash commit with main as its only parent.

Between A and B come a records-only commit and an intervention commit (paths as at tests.rs:3982). C's PR head is its landing commit.
